title: He comes, pale vampire, through storm his eyes, his bat sails bloodying the sea, mouth to her mouth’s kiss.
html_source:
Some of the most poetic sunset imagery ever here. The moon here being personified as masculine, but frail (“pale vampire”), and the sun as feminine, and strong (she “trascines her load” and is a “flaming sword” by contrast).

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Compare this with how the poem is rendered in chapter 7:

On swift sail flaming
From storm and south
He comes, pale vampire,
Mouth to my mouth.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: From Douglas Hyde’s ‘My Grief on the Sea’:

And my love came behind me—
He came from the South;
His breast to my bosom,
His mouth to my mouth.

Possibly hinting at Stephen’s frustration in not being able to distinguish himself (so far) as a poet, and therefore shaping sounds from other’s work.
